slides.title: **5 AI myths** keeping you stuck doing busywork
slides.sub: Each one busted with a real example you can try today.

messages.text: I'm a plumber. Write a text telling Mrs. Patel I'm running 20 minutes late. Friendly, short.
Hi Mrs. Patel, it's [YOUR NAME] the plumber. I'm running about 20 minutes late, sorry about that. I'll be with you as soon as I can.

slides.note: **Reality:** that's the whole skill. Plain English in, a usable draft out. (Example names invented.)

slides.kicker: Myth 2: "AI always sounds like a robot"

before.label: NO EXAMPLE GIVEN
before.text: Thank you for reaching out! Yes, we are open on Saturday from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM. We look forward to seeing you!

after.label: + "SOUND LIKE ME" + ONE OLD MESSAGE
after.text: Hey! Yep, we're open Saturday, 9 till 1. Pop in whenever suits, and shout if you want anything put aside.

slides.note: **Reality:** it only sounds generic when you give it nothing to copy. Same question both times: open Saturday? (Yes, 9 to 1.)

slides.title: "It'll do the job **for me**."
paras: **Reality:** it writes the first draft, fast. You still make the calls.
Check names, prices, dates and anything you're promising before it goes out. AI can sound sure and still be wrong.

slides.kicker: Myth 4: "I need a big setup first"
slides.title: Reality: start with **one task**

caption:
5 AI myths that keep small business owners stuck doing busywork (and what's actually true)

Myth 1: you need to be techy. You don't. If you can text, you can write a prompt.

Myth 2: it sounds like a robot. Only when you give it nothing to copy. Try this:

"Reply to this message: [PASTE]. Sound like me. Here's a message I wrote last week: [PASTE ONE OF YOUR MESSAGES]"

Myth 3: it does the job for you. It writes the first draft. You check names, prices, dates and promises.

Myth 4: you need a big setup. Start with one task you dread and one saved prompt.

Myth 5: it's just for social posts. It's best at the boring stuff: inbox, quotes, weekly plans, summaries.
